newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish debt to GDP ratio to drop in 1997-Caruana.
newsitem.headline: Spanish debt to GDP ratio to drop in 1997-Caruana.

text.p: Spain will reduce its debt to GDP ratio by 1.3 percentage points in 1997, making further progress towards meeting the criteria for a single currency, Treasury General Director Jaime Caruana said.

"In debt to GDP we are not going to be below 60 percent, but we are going to shrink by more than one percentage point, or 1.3 points, approximately, with which we would fulfil the second version of the debt criteria, reduction," Caruana said in an interview with financial daily Gaceta de Negocios published on Monday.
Countries which join the launch of European economic and moentary union in January 1999 must have a debt to GDP ratio of 60 percent or be seen to be approaching that level at a satisfactory pace.
Caruana gave no further details on the expected 1997 level, but Spain's debt to GDP ratio ended 1996 at 69.3 percent.
Nations joining the single currency are also expected to reduce their budget deficits to three percent of GDP.
"In the deficit, our objective of three percent will be reached. The doubt is whether we will remain a little below three percent," Caruana said.

Caruana said Spanish interest rates could continue to fall given the need to converge with a short-term German rate that now stands at 3.00 percent. The key Spanish money market rate now stands at 5.25 percent.
"We believe that rates will decline when the market considers that they should," he said.
Currently, some 42 to 43 percent of Spanish bonds -- which represent 50 percent of the country's debt -- bears interest rates of more than 10 percent.

Of a total issuing requirement this year of some 20 trillion pesetas gross, the Treasury must still issue a little less than nine trillion pesetas. In net terms, some 1.6 trillion must still be issued, Caruana said.
With respect to the peseta, Caruana said it could enter the euro with a rate of some 84.20 to 85.07 to the mark.
"It has to be refined, but we are talking about a very narrow range, equivalent to an exhange rate against the mark of 84.20 to 85.07," Caruana said.
The peseta was trading at 84.30/33 to the mark early on Monday.
